Lessons.Title: Evaluating Logarithmic Expressions
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Calculate the value of a logarithmic expression using estimation or technology. Justify (orally) why one logarithmic expression is greater than another.
Logarithms measure exponents. For b>1, larger positive arguments give larger log values; for 0<b<1 order reverses. Exact powers avoid needless approximations.

Source activity 11.1: Math Talk: Finding Values: \(\log \frac{1}{1,000}\) Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 11.2: Log War!: Have you played the game of war with a deck of playing cards? Your teacher will give you and your partner a set of special cards. Shuffle and deal the cards evenly. Each player turns one card face up. The card with the greater value wins the round and its player captures both cards and sets them aside. If you and your partner disagree about the value of a card, discuss until… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 11.3: Finding Logarithms with a Calculator: Experiment with your calculator until you understand how to evaluate \(\log_{10} 19\). What value do you see on the calculator? Discuss with a partner: Why might \(\log_{10} 19\) be expressed in different ways? To solve the equation \(10^m= 19\), Tyler writes the equation in the logarithmic form: \(m = \log_{10} 19\). He then presses the “log” button on the calculator, enters… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Practice Problem 1: Select all expressions that are equal to \(\log_2 8\). \(\log_{10} 1,\!000\) \(\log_{10} 0.001\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 2: Which expression has a greater value: \(\log_{10} \frac {1}{100}\) or \(\log_2 \frac {1}{8}\)? Explain how you know. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: Andre says that \(\log_{10}(55) = 1.5\) because 55 is halfway between 10 and 100. Do you agree with Andre? Explain your reasoning. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: An exponential function is defined by \(k(x)= 15 \boldcdot 2^x\). Show that when \(x\) increases from 1 to 1.25 and when it increases from 2.75 to 3, the value of \(k\) grows by the same factor. Show that when \(x\) increases from \(t\) to \(t+0.25\), \(k(t)\) also grows by this same factor. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 5: How many times does $1 need to double in value to become $1,000,000? Explain how you know. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 6: What values could replace the “?” in these equations to make them true? \(\log_{10} 10,\!000 = {?}\) \(\log_{10} 10,\!000,\!000 = {?}\) \(\log_{10} {?} = 5\) \(\log_{10} {?} = 1\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 7: What value of \(t\) would make the equation \(2^t = 6\) true? Between which two whole numbers is the value of \(\log_2 6\)? Explain how you know. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 8: For each exponential equation, write an equivalent equation in logarithmic form. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Edulytics independent cool-down: Is log_2(16) bigger than log_2(8)? Find both. Expected reasoning or answer: 4>3.
